intro.title: Welcome to Midelt — apples and the Middle Atlas
intro.p1: Midelt sits high in the Middle Atlas, known for its apple orchards, cooler air and its role as a stop on the classic road between Fez (or Meknes) and Errachidia toward the desert. The landscape mixes irrigated fruit valleys with open mountain approaches.
intro.p2: Plan one night for a quiet mountain break, or two if you add the Cirque de Jaffar excursion. It is practical more than polished — ideal for travellers who want altitude, orchards and a slower pace between imperial cities and the south.

apples.title: Apple country
apples.p1: Midelt is closely tied to apple growing: irrigated orchards in the surrounding valleys produce much of the fruit associated with this high Middle Atlas town.
apples.p2: Seasonal activity peaks around harvest. Roadside stands and local markets are the simplest way to taste the region’s produce.
apples.tip: Autumn harvest is the most photogenic and animated time among the trees.

centre.title: Town centre & souk
centre.p1: Midelt’s centre is a working mountain hub: cafés, shops, transport and a souk that serves the plateau more than tourists.
centre.p2: Use it to restock and eat between orchard drives and any Cirque de Jaffar day. Market energy varies by day — ask on arrival.
centre.tip: Good base for a coffee after arriving from Fez or before the desert road south.

jaffar.title: Cirque de Jaffar
jaffar.p1: The Cirque de Jaffar is a wide natural amphitheatre in the mountains south of Midelt — open views, dramatic walls and a sense of scale that rewards a half- or full-day outing.
jaffar.p2: Road conditions vary; a 4x4 or experienced local driver is often recommended. Check weather and access before setting out.
jaffar.tip: Start early for clearer light and more time on the tracks.

foothills.title: Middle Atlas approaches
foothills.p1: Around Midelt the land rises and opens: cooler air, long views and the first real feel of the Middle Atlas plateau and ridges.
foothills.p2: Short roadside stops are enough for most itineraries; serious hiking starts deeper into the range.
foothills.tip: Layers help — altitude can feel cool even when the plains are hot.

valley.title: Irrigated valleys
valley.p1: Green ribbons of orchards and small plots cut through drier hills — the irrigated landscape that makes Midelt productive at altitude.
valley.p2: Drive or walk the valley edges with respect for private land and irrigation channels.
valley.tip: Morning light on the fruit trees is soft and clear.

road.title: Fez–Errachidia road stop
road.p1: Midelt sits on the classic inland route linking the north (Fez, Meknes) with Errachidia and the desert approaches — many travellers overnight here to break the drive.
road.p2: Services are geared to transit as much as sightseeing; book ahead in peak seasons.
road.tip: Ideal halfway pause if you are not rushing straight to Merzouga.

card3.name: Simple road-stop hotel
card3.desc: Clean overnight for the Fez–Errachidia leg — practical if Midelt is one night between imperial cities and the desert.

timing.title: When to come
timing.desc: Spring and autumn are mild. Summer is cooler than the plains but can still be strong at midday; winter is quiet and cold.

q1.question: How long should I stay in Midelt?
q1.answer: One night breaks the Fez–Errachidia drive; two nights if you add Cirque de Jaffar or want orchard time.

q2.question: What is Cirque de Jaffar?
q2.answer: A large natural mountain amphitheatre south of Midelt, reached by mountain tracks — often done as a day trip with a suitable vehicle.

q3.question: How do I get to Midelt?
q3.answer: By road from Fez or Meknes (about 3–3.5h) or Errachidia (about 2.5–3h). Buses and grands taxis serve the corridor.

q4.question: Why is Midelt known for apples?
q4.answer: Irrigated valleys around the town support extensive apple orchards — a signature of this high Middle Atlas stop.

itinerary.title: Suggested 2–3 Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan for orchards, mountain air and Cirque de Jaffar.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Settle in, café in the centre, short orientation walk.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Drive or taxi to the irrigated orchards for light and local produce.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Tagine or grill and an early night at altitude.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Early departure toward the amphitheatre with suitable transport.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Time at the viewpoints, then back to Midelt.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Simple dinner and rest after the mountain tracks.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Coffee and a last look at the plateau light.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Continue north toward Fez/Meknes or south toward Errachidia and the desert.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Overnight in your next city depending on the route.
